               Quarterly Activities Report
                         For the period of three months ending 30 September 2026
Highlights
Koppamurra: pilot plant commissioned at ANSTO with first Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide produced
    ▪   Pilot plant commissioning completed on 31 July 2026 at ANSTO's critical minerals facility in Sydney, with
     AR3 the first industry partner to use the purpose-built, clay-hosted rare earth pilot processing plant (refer
     ASX announcement "Koppamurra Pilot Processing Underway" 11 August 2026).
    ▪  Continuous pilot processing of ~30 tonnes of Koppamurra ore underway. The first of four heap leach column
       cycles (~8 tonnes) was completed, generating ~5,000 L of Pregnant Leach Solution (PLS) at target leaching
      recovery rates.
    ▪   First PLS batch processed through the continuous precipitation circuit to produce a Mixed Rare Earth
      Hydroxide (MREOH), marking the transition from rare earth extraction to a concentrated intermediate
      product. The MREOH will be refined into Mixed Rare Earth Oxide (MREO) samples for customer qualification
       (refer ASX announcement "Koppamurra Pilot Plant Advances to Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide Production"
     10 September 2026).
    ▪  The pilot campaign is generating the engineering and operating data required for Definitive Feasibility Study
      (DFS) design which will commence early 2027.
    ▪  Mining Lease Application preparation continuing, with submission targeted for the end of 2026.
Overland Project: carbonatite discovery extended ~5 km south with 130m intersection
    ▪  Niobium–rare earth carbonatite system identified at the R254 prospect: OV167 returned 19m @ 0.61%
     TREO from 86m to end of hole, including 7m @ 0.56% TREO with 0.27% Nb₂O₅ from 86m. Pyrochlore, the
       principal niobium ore mineral, was identified (refer ASX announcement 8 July 2026).
    ▪  A 10 km north–south magnetic corridor was delineated from reprocessed airborne magnetic data,
       materially expanding the drill target inventory beyond OV167 (refer ASX announcement 23 July 2026).
    ▪  A follow-up aircore program commenced on 1 September 2026 across five traverses of the magnetic
       corridor.
    ▪  OV176 intersected 130m (downhole) of interpreted carbonatite from 68m, ending in carbonatite at 201m,
      approximately 5 km south of OV167. Assays are pending (refer ASX announcement "AR3 expands Overland
      carbonatite discovery" 15 September 2026
Corporate
    ▪  A $2.1 million instalment received under the Australian Government's International Partnerships in Critical
      Minerals (IPCM) Program, taking cumulative receipts to $4.85 million of the Company's $5 million award
       (refer ASX announcement 28 August 2026).
    ▪  Koppamurra was included in the Australian Government’s Critical Minerals Prospectus which profiles
      investment-ready projects, including 58 upstream projects (Subsequent to the quarter). The prospectus
      helps to facilitate international investment in the critical minerals sector.
    ▪  Investor engagement during the quarter included a non-deal east coast roadshow in July 2026 and

Australian Rare Earths Limited (AR3 or the Company) is pleased to provide an update on progress made during
the quarter ended 30 September 2026.

Operational Review
AR3 advanced both of its key projects during the September quarter. At Koppamurra, pilot-scale processing at
ANSTO moved through commissioning into continuous operation, with the first batch of Pregnant Leach Solution
processed through to a Mixed Rare Earth Hydroxide intermediate product. At Overland, the niobium–rare earth
carbonatite discovery progressed from a single drill hole to a corridor-scale exploration program, with follow-up
drilling intersecting interpreted carbonatite over 130 metres (downhole) approximately 5 km south of the original
discovery hole.

Koppamurra Rare Earths Project, South Australia
Following delivery of the Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) and maiden Ore Reserve in June 2026, activity at Koppamurra
during the quarter focused on pilot-scale processing at ANSTO's critical minerals facility in Sydney. The program is
designed to validate AR3's processing flowsheet at pilot scale, generate engineering data to support Definitive
Feasibility Study (DFS) design, and produce Mixed Rare Earth Oxide (MREO) samples for prospective customers
and offtake partners. The program  is co-funded under the Company's $5 million Australian Government
International Partnerships in Critical Minerals (IPCM) grant.

Pilot Plant Commissioned and Continuous Processing Underway
Commissioning of the pilot plant was completed on 31 July 2026 using approximately 1 tonne of Koppamurra ore,
with AR3 the first industry partner to use ANSTO's purpose-built, clay-hosted rare earth pilot processing plant
(refer ASX announcement "Koppamurra Pilot Processing Underway" 11 August 2026). Commissioning confirmed
the design basis for key operating parameters, including agglomerate preparation, irrigation flow rates and
lixiviant make-up requirements, and validated the column loading and irrigation approach. Commissioning
outcomes included:
    ▪  Production of 940 kg of on-specification agglomerates.
    ▪  Seamless loading of the columns.
    ▪   Irrigation at above design rates with no degradation of flow.
    ▪  Rare earth recovery in line with expectations.
Following commissioning, the Company commenced pilot processing of approximately 30 tonnes of Koppamurra
ore. The program targets completion of four cycles of the eight 4-metre columns to recover rare earths from the
ore, with liquor from each cycle to be processed downstream into the projects final product, Mixed Rare Earth
Oxide.
